doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Classical training at Mastbaum and the Philharmonic
summary: He trained classically at the Mastbaum School, discusses limited concert opportunities for black musicians and how classical focus stiffened his jazz, and subbed with the New York Philharmonic.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Great. And were you classically trained as a musician? You had classical training?
Oh, yeah. I had a lot of classical training. I went to the Mastbaum School in Philadelphia with Buddy DeFranco and Red Rodney, and a bunch of guys. And John LaPorta.
Oh yeah. What were the opportunities like back at that time for a musician such as yourself?

Well the opportunities for black musicians in the concert field were nil, I mean they just weren’t there. And you sort of, I was still interested in classical music and because of that I guess I studied pretty hard at what I was doing at the time and I guess it gave me a little more momentum when I became a commercial player, it was a big help to me, discipline- wise and things like that. But I must say because of having more interest at that point in classical music when I was younger, it inhibited my jazz playing a great deal because I just didn’t feel comfortable and I didn’t play very well actually. I was very stiff. Now, in later years of course I’ve been doing more of that and I feel more relaxed with it and probably play a little better at it. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-
You sound like you play a lot better at it today. And you’ve played with the New York Philharmonic?

I subbed with them a few times with Boulez was there and when Kostelanetz was there. And usually there was times when they were doing “The Pines of Rome” and they added a couple of extra trumpets or something.
